# Resident native application process

The Rust `mluva` executable now owns the assembled application, its theme, native I/O runtime and shutdown. It uses the released `com.mluva.Linux` application identity and registers all actions before activation. Normal launch initializes local stores and the window once; service launch waits without opening a window. A second invocation forwards to the first process. Resources resolve from the relocated executable's `../resources` directory, with no checkout or Python fallback. The exact `--narrate` invocation dispatches before GTK startup or resource loading.

The immutable reference is Mluva v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. [The process fixture](released-bootstrap.json), SHA-256 `120eaf3f25719658745d02f5207f5860237335a21bcd462eb0bd02f25c5ef12a`, records eight actual released processes, 38 public states, all 13 action descriptors and five command-line cases. The external observer verifies every released module against the commit and launches the unchanged module entry point. It observes the real application name owner, `org.gtk.Actions`, both recording-status signals, window visibility, public accessible names/roles and list order. Repeated identical snapshots are stored once; observations are not generated from the native implementation.

The cases cover background status/global-record/Meeting/Personalization without activation; cold Latest, History, Settings and Commands; normal startup and welcome; missing speech credentials; navigation and command-palette contents/order; Escape, close-to-hide and hidden actions; second-process reopening; and normal/cold Quit. The second process receives different, empty XDG paths: it exits successfully, leaves them empty and preserves the first D-Bus owner. Help, unsupported options, headless Incognito narration and an invalid mixed narration invocation match exit status and exact output. Only the reference help's executable basename, `app.py`, is normalized to `mluva`.

One released bug is retained explicitly in the fixture's diagnostics: quitting a cold service logs an `AttributeError` for the uninitialized scratchpad while returning status 0. The native test requires the same exit and no window, with empty diagnostics. This is a deliberate cleanup repair, not a claimed byte-identical traceback. All other reference process logs and all native process logs are empty; the retained runs have no accessibility warnings.

[The first-record fixture](released-bootstrap-record.json), SHA-256 `8942e5472a83d6e801b2783042c22bc1e4165dbc012c0915165e17dc4997c755`, separately observes a real cold `record` action. It compares the recording window's accessible content, actual preparing/recording phase order, the last observed status/shell pair, PCM child arguments, exit, child disappearance, empty retained audio/History, unchanged clipboard and zero loopback-provider requests after Quit. Elapsed display/seconds and sampled audio level are labeled `$SAMPLED`; repeated timer publications are excluded from the final pair. All other fields remain exact. The PCM is synthetic, and the provider is a private loopback server.

That comparison first reproduced a dropped native Record action: asynchronous startup had not installed capture services when the action arrived. A cold Record now preserves one startup request until the current readiness generation succeeds. Cancellation, another toggle, initialization failure or shutdown clears it. Three additional native process faults cover Cancel and repeated Record while a separate credential process is delayed, plus startup with missing resources. Both delayed cases wait for the public Dictate button to become sensitive and verify that no microphone ever starts. Missing resources fail with a bounded, redacted error and no data files. Quit joins the same idempotent cleanup whether requested through an action or the GApplication shutdown signal.

The comparison also found and repaired hidden Meeting/Personalization actions showing the window, extra feature-maturity commands, wrong preference-command ordering and a missing initial hidden-status publication. The full command palette now starts its preference index with Prompts and omits the informational feature-maturity page, as the reference does. Visible settings navigation retains its separate order.

The maintained Rust process test stages actual ELF binaries and resources in its private directory, changes its working directory and uses public interfaces only. It shares the public accessibility transport with the real editor test. The existing [24-case narration comparison](../../../mluva-workflows/tests/fixtures/narration-evidence.md) was run through both `mluva-narrate` and `mluva --narrate`, with DISPLAY/session/accessibility variables removed from each child. Both paths also pass its three cancellation/initialization faults. The real Tensaku PNG/OCR, Cancel, Save and Undo/Redo test was repeated after sharing the observer.

Build the ordinary native process dependencies, then run the explicit process acceptance:

```sh
cargo build --locked -p mluva-gtk --bin mluva \
  -p mluva-audio --bin mluva-audio-cleanup --bin audio-fixture-peer \
  -p mluva-providers --bin credential-fixture-peer
bash dev/run-isolated-browser.sh tmp/native-bootstrap -- \
  cargo test --locked -p mluva-gtk --test bootstrap -- --ignored --test-threads=1 --nocapture
bash dev/run-isolated-browser.sh tmp/native-main-narration -- \
  env MLUVA_TEST_APP_NARRATION=/absolute/path/to/cargo-target/debug/mluva \
  cargo test --locked -p mluva-workflows --test narration -- --ignored --test-threads=1 --nocapture
```

The runner isolates DISPLAY, session/accessibility buses, HOME/XDG, network/PID/mount namespaces and host input/audio/GPU devices. Actual input remains in private Xvfb/Openbox. No host focus, pointer, clipboard, microphone, managed credentials or user-content upload is used. Reference observers and raw receipts remain under ignored `tmp/`; native acceptance requires no Python. The combined narration/editor run is retained in `tmp/bootstrap-final-evidence/` and `tmp/bootstrap-final-acceptance.log`. After moving preference-index ownership into the application, the process comparison passed again in `tmp/bootstrap-reviewed-evidence/` and `tmp/bootstrap-reviewed-acceptance.log`.

Workspace checks pass 137 ordinary tests with 40 environment-dependent checks ignored. The process, both narration paths, real editor, assembled application, screenshot ownership and command/window comparisons were explicitly executed. The command component keeps the caller's ordered page list; the full application separately supplies its released seven-page index. The shortcut regression also passes all eight workflows/34 states and its readiness fault with clean diagnostics after giving each scenario a fresh client process; [its evidence](application-shortcuts-evidence.md) records that harness correction. Strict all-target Clippy and formatting/diff checks pass. Earlier failed or warning-bearing runs are diagnostic material, not accepted evidence.

This establishes a runnable resident development executable and bounded startup/action/narration behavior. It does not establish final installation, native managed-credential launcher or shell watcher, real Wayland/Omarchy widget/compositor behavior, all joined editor/application/provider paths, physical devices, complete visual/scale/platform parity or performance gains. Packaging, removal of all maintained/shipped Python and complete acceptance remain required. The installed app/widget remain v1.6.0 and all complete-workflow parity rows remain Pending.
